doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Earl Hines and Gerald Wiggins
summary: Hines's trumpet-style piano and Wiggins as an underrated accompanist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Earl Hines was a marvelous leader. I didn’t have an opportunity to work too much with Gates, except on a couple of occasions with a small group, after he had Marva [Josie], the singer, and Budd Johnson was with him at the time. But he was a nice man, a great musician. I’m very proud of the fact that he got Louis Armstrong involved in – with his playing, or Louis got him involved. They inspired each other. But
Louis played – Earl played what they call the trumpet-style on piano. He was a good musician.
I hear that, but what does that mean, the trumpet-style on piano?
It means [Terry sings] arpeggio-style [he sings further]. A single thing [he sings] instead of [he sings] a chord progression.

Gerald Wiggins is a marvelous accompanist, a great pianist, and underrated like hell. He’ll play – he’ll swing you into bad health. He’s a good player, and his little boy plays great bass, little Junior, whatever his name is.
